newsitem.title: USA: Missouri corn 31 pct harvested, matches average.
newsitem.headline: Missouri corn 31 pct harvested, matches average.

text.p: Missouri's corn crop was harvested on 31 percent of the acreage, matching the five year average and ahead of last year's 24 percent as of Sunday, according to the Missouri Agricultural Statistics Service.
Corn crop condition was rated one percent very poor, six percent poor, 24 percent fair, 47 percent good and 22 percent excellent.
Development of the soybean crop was similar to last year but about five days behind the average pace, the Statistics Service said.
Soybean conditions were two percent very poor, eight percent poor, 33 percent fair, 46 percent good and 11 percent excellent.

The soybean crop rated mature on 19 percent of the acreage, compared with 12 percent last year and the 30 percent average. Soybeans were dropping leaves on 38 percent of the crop, compared with 40 percent last year and 56 percent for the average.
Twenty-one percent of the cotton crop was harvested, six days ahead of last year's 11 percent and five days ahead of the 13 percent average.

Eighty-seven percent of the cotton crop was opening bolls, eight days ahead of last year's average of 78 percent and about nine days ahead of the average pace of 75 percent. Cotton was one percent very poor, nine percent poor, 25 percent fair, 60 percent good and five percent excellent.
Six percent of the winter wheat crop was seeded, behind the previous year and the average pace of nine percent.
